title: Ionic Memory and Computing
intro: This research examines how ionic materials process, retain, and transmit information, toward principles for energy-efficient computing.
caption: Conceptual comparison of biological neurons, software-based artificial neurons, and ionic approaches to information processing. The schematic illustrates different ways to represent signal transmission and nonlinear response; it does not depict a completed computing device.
background_html: A 2026 reference scenario projects that data centers could consume nearly 12% of U.S. electricity by 2030. The human brain operates on roughly 20 watts. (Smith et al., 2026; Levy & Calvert, 2021).
alt: Biological neuron above a software neuron model and a conceptual ionic circuit with artificial synapses and nonlinear transport.

title: Selective Ion Transport
intro: This research examines the molecular basis of selective transport, with the goal of separating valuable elements using fewer resources and generating less waste.
caption: Lanmodulin and K⁺ channels illustrate biological ion coordination alongside a conceptual synthetic nanopore for rare-earth separation through entry, binding, and release. The Nd³⁺/Dy³⁺ contrast is illustrative and does not report measured separation performance.
background_html: In 2024, 91% of the world’s refined magnet rare earths came from a single country. Their chemical similarity makes separation difficult, limiting routes to more resilient supply chains. (IEA, 2026).
alt: Lanmodulin and a potassium channel with enlarged ion-coordination sites beside a synthetic nanopore showing rare-earth-ion entry, binding, and release.

title: Interfacial Molecular Recognition
intro: This research studies molecular recognition at interfaces to extend continuous sensing beyond glucose and make molecular measurements more accessible.
caption: Molecular recognition in olfaction and electrochemical biosensing. The enlarged views compare target binding by a biological receptor with binding by an electrode-tethered recognition element. The sensing electrode is shown in a tissue setting to illustrate a potential route to physiological monitoring.
background_html: A 2021 Lancet Commission estimated that 47% of the world’s population had little or no access to diagnostics. Continuous glucose monitors demonstrate the value of molecular measurements beyond the laboratory. (Fleming et al., 2021).
alt: Olfactory receptors and a tissue-mounted sensing electrode, with enlarged views of molecular binding in biological and electrode-tethered receptors.

title: AI/ML Automation
background_html: In a survey of 1,972 scientists, respondents reported spending, on average, 30% of their working time developing scientific software and 40% using it (Hannay et al., 2009).
intro: This research aims to reduce the hands-on workload of molecular simulation through AI-assisted automation, while keeping scientific judgment with the researcher.
caption: Computation-guided experimental discovery. Candidates and screening outcomes are illustrative, not reported results. The robotic arms represent software-based automation, not physical laboratory robots.
alt: Conceptual illustration linking researcher direction, computational automation, illustrative candidate screening, and experimental studies.
